simpleqa_verified.summary: 1,000 short fact-seeking questions (Google DeepMind 2025 cleanup of OpenAI SimpleQA: de-duplicated, topic-balanced, labels re-checked), with topic, answer type and source URLs, graded by an autorater (F1). It is the Yugos live set, so only the ~950 questions outside the 50-question live sample are usable as router training data.
sources: local copy /root/cic/sn34-yugos/research/benchmarks/catalog/simpleqa_verified (1,000 rows; median question 90 characters)

chat.why: Three-option multiple choice on social commonsense (motives, reactions) after a one-sentence context: MC answer like mmlu_pro, but the topic (everyday social situations) is far from Yugos's knowledge and reasoning-puzzle mix.

math_code.why: different skill: social commonsense, no math or code

social_iqa.summary: About 35k three-choice questions (33,410 train + 1,954 validation; test labels on the AI2 leaderboard) asking how people feel or why they act in short social scenes (EMNLP 2019). Easy, old and heavily trained on; at most a filler for the very easy private chat part. Per-question correctness for 112 open 2024 models is inside EmbedLLM (SocialQA).

chat.why: Read one Wikipedia paragraph and extract a short answer (or say unanswerable, ~50% of validation), scored by F1/EM: a single-hop version of the hotpotqa task with the same kind of checker.

math_code.why: different skill: reading comprehension, no math or code

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, no function calls, one plain text question

squad.summary: SQuAD 2.0 (2018): 130,319 train + 11,873 validation questions on Wikipedia paragraphs (median paragraph+question ~780 characters), about half of validation unanswerable; Yugos's catalog grades it with F1 on validation. Old and heavily trained on, so mostly easy L1-L2 reading questions that could stand in for easy private chat items.
sources: inspect_evals squad README; yugos_evals catalog.py (squad: scorer f1, SQuAD v2 validation)

strategyqa.summary: StrategyQA (TACL 2021, 2,780 questions; this HF copy is the 2,290 official-train questions re-split 1,603/687) with term, facts and boolean answer. Easy-to-medium closed-book reasoning; label noise caps scores (paper: humans 87%), so frontier models do not reach 100%.

chat.why: Graduate-level multiple choice with ~10 options (avg 9.67) across 285 subfields, letter answer: the same shape as mmlu_pro and the MC part of hle, and hard enough for L3-L4.

math_code.why: Some questions are calculations (engineering, science, math subfields) but answered by picking a letter, not a boxed closed-form answer or code.

supergpqa.overlap: Card says a limited portion is derived from other datasets including MMLU-Pro (live mmlu_pro) and OpenAI simple-evals short-form factuality (SimpleQA, the source of simpleqa_verified); size of that portion not stated, so de-duplicate against both before use.
supergpqa.summary: 26,529 graduate-level 4-10 option questions in 13 disciplines / 285 subfields (Feb 2025), with difficulty labels (easy/middle/hard) and an is_calculation flag. Best large public stand-in for mmlu_pro/hle-style chat questions, and SuperGPQA-Records gives per-question responses and correct/incorrect status for 49 zero-shot models (GPT-4o x3, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, o1, o3-mini, DeepSeek-R1/V3, Llama 3.1 8B-405B, Qwen2.5, Gemma 2...) plus 26 base models.

chat.why: Closed-book trivia questions with a short answer and alias list (EM): the same skill as simpleqa_verified factual recall, but easier and much older; the rc configs add very long evidence documents, so use nocontext.

math_code.why: different skill: trivia recall, no math or code

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, no function calls, one plain text question

triviaqa.licence: unknown (card: University of Washington does not own the copyright of the questions and documents)
triviaqa.summary: TriviaQA (2017): about 95K trivia question-answer pairs (rc split 138,384 train / 17,944 validation / 17,210 test rows) with answer aliases and optional Wikipedia/web evidence. Huge supply of easy factual-recall questions for the easy private chat part; too easy and too memorised to mimic simpleqa_verified's hard tail.

chat.why: Yugos catalog runs the mc1 config: a factual question built to trigger common misconceptions, pick the single true option (letter answer, avg 5 options); MC fact questions like mmlu_pro/simpleqa but a narrow adversarial topic set.

math_code.why: different skill: misconception-resistant factual QA, no math or code

truthfulqa.summary: 817 questions in 38 categories (health, law, misconceptions...), 2021, in generation and multiple-choice configs; Yugos's catalog uses mc1 (one true answer among 2-13 options, mean 5). Tiny, famous and trained against, so only a small easy-chat filler; per-question outcomes exist in HELM Classic and EmbedLLM for old models.
sources: inspect_evals truthfulqa README; yugos_evals catalog.py (target mc1)

two_wiki_multihop.summary: 192,606 template-generated multi-hop questions (COLING 2020; train 167,454 / dev 12,576 / test 12,576 with hidden answers) of four types: compositional 45%, comparison 30%, bridge-comparison 21%, inference 4%. The best large stand-in for Yugos's hotpotqa questions (same input and grading shape), though the templated wording is narrower.

web_questions.summary: WebQuestions (EMNLP 2013): 5,810 rows (3,778 train / 2,032 test) of lower-case one-line questions with Freebase answer lists. Very old, easy and memorised; gold answers are dated (Freebase is shut down), so it is a weak filler for easy factual chat.

chat.why: Real user conversations with ChatGPT (~41% multi-turn, ~53% English turns) with no reference answer or grade, so capped like preference prompts; useful only as realistic prompt text, not as checkable questions.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, no function calls, one plain text question

wildchat.licence: odc-by (hub); the 2024 paper says it was first released under AI2 ImpACT licences
wildchat.summary: 837,989 logged user conversations (collected Apr 2023 - May 2024) with GPT-3.5-Turbo (~76%) and GPT-4 (~24%), 74 languages, average user turn ~296 tokens with a long tail. No answers or quality labels, so it cannot teach the router who is right; at most a source of realistic prompt styles for the unseen private chat part.
languages: multilingual (74 language classes; about 53% of turns English)

winogrande.summary: WinoGrande (2019): ~44k two-option fill-the-blank commonsense sentences (xl: 40,398 train / 1,267 validation / 1,767 test with hidden labels); Yugos's catalog runs winogrande_xl 0-shot. Near-saturated by 2024 flagships, so it can only add easy L1-L2 items to the private-chat style mix.
sources: inspect_evals winogrande README; yugos_evals catalog.py (winogrande_xl, fewshot 0)

worldsense.summary: Meta's WorldSense (Nov 2023): 87,048 synthetic test trials (Infer / Consistency / Completion, trivial vs normal, 3-5 objects, ~100-token prompts) answered with a fixed option; a 1M-trial training set also exists. In Yugos's catalog; a cheap, controllable source of easy-to-medium reasoning items, with per-question responses for 3 old models.

zebralogic.results_where: https://github.com/WildEval/ZeroEval/tree/main/result_dirs/zebra-grid (~69 per-model result files up to o1, o3-mini, DeepSeek-R1, grok-3)
zebralogic.summary: 1,000 logic grid puzzles (40 per size, 25 sizes) plus 3,259 multiple-choice cell questions (2024; paper Feb 2025), prompts ~100-700 tokens, puzzle-level exact accuracy. A good stand-in for bbeh-style hard reasoning with a clean difficulty knob (grid size), and per-model outputs for ~69 models are public; mind that some 2025 models report 90%+ (likely trained on such puzzles).
sources: local BBEH copy (zebra puzzles task uses a different generator: 7-8 people in a row)

chat.why: Mix of 10 benchmarks, mostly multiple choice (MMLU, TruthfulQA, SocialIQA, PIQA, MedMCQA, LogiQA, GPQA, MathQA), single prompt with few-shot text; correctness from lm-eval-harness, close to Yugos's easy MC chat questions.

math_code.why: GSM8K, ASDiv and MathQA give grade-school math word problems (numeric or MC answer); no competition math or code.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, no function calls, one plain text question

level_guess.why: Component benchmarks are 2019-2023 classics: 8B-class models score ~0.6-0.85 raw (Llama-3-8B-Instruct MMLU 0.66, SIQA 0.73, PIQA 0.77; Llama 3.1 8B GSM8K 0.85, GPQA 0.30) before removing 25-50% MC guessing, and GPT-4-class models ~0.85-0.95 (GPT-4 MMLU 0.864, GSM8K 0.92); GPQA is the only hard part (~9% of questions).

embedllm.results_where: https://huggingface.co/datasets/RZ412/EmbedLLM (train/val/test.csv: binary correct label per model x question)
embedllm.summary: Router data set (Oct 2024): binary correctness of 112 open Hugging Face models (0.5B-72B, newest Llama-3-70B-Instruct, Qwen1.5, Mistral-7B-Instruct, Gemma-7B-it, Yi-34B, Vicuna...) on 36,054 test questions from MMLU, TruthfulQA, SocialIQA, PIQA, MedMCQA, MathQA, LogiQA, GSM8K, GPQA and ASDiv (lm-eval-harness). Good for pre-training question difficulty / IRT on easy MC chat, but no API, frontier or 2025+ models, no cost or tokens, and no live Yugos set.

chat.why: Mix of single-prompt QA scenarios with references (Capabilities: MMLU-Pro, GPQA, IFEval, WildBench; Lite: NaturalQuestions, NarrativeQA, OpenbookQA, MMLU, LegalBench, MedQA; Classic: many more), graded by EM/MC/judge; overlaps chat closely but includes translation, long stories and judge-only items.

math_code.why: Math part (MATH and GSM8K in Lite/Classic, Omni-MATH in Capabilities) matches math_code with checked final answers; almost no code.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, no function calls, one plain text question

helm_raw.results_where: https://storage.googleapis.com/crfm-helm-public/ (per_instance_stats.json + display_predictions.json per run; Capabilities v1.15.0 (2025-11-24): 68 models x 5 scenarios incl. GPT-5, GPT-5.1, Gemini 3 Pro preview, Claude Sonnet 4.5; Lite v1.13.0: 91 models; Classic v0.4.0: 70 older models)
helm_raw.overlap: HELM Capabilities runs 1,000 sampled MMLU-Pro questions (live mmlu_pro) and HELM Lite/Classic run MATH (live math set): drop those questions or keep them out of any test split.
helm_raw.summary: Router data set: Stanford HELM's public bucket with per-instance predictions and scores for many models. Most useful slice is Capabilities v1.15.0 (MMLU-Pro 1,000, GPQA 446, IFEval 541, WildBench 1,000, Omni-MATH 1,000) for 68 models up to GPT-5.1 and Gemini 3 Pro preview, plus Lite (91 models to GPT-4o / Claude 3.5) and Classic (old models); no Nov-2026 frontier, no tool use. Image/audio projects (VHELM, AHELM, HEIM) must be skipped.
